text: They are required to show why they should not be bound over for disturbing the peace and for inciting a breach of the peace. The summonses say they are 'likely to persevere in such unlawful conduct.' Lord Russell, 89, was putting his affairs in order, and packing a case, at his Chelsea home yesterday. His secretary, American-born Mr. Ralph Schoenman, said: 'They require him to show why he should not be bound over for disturbing the peace. For what? For inciting a breach of the peace. Putting us off our order and packing a case at Lord Russell's Chelsea home yesterday.'
